'''Timothy D. Lash''' (born 13 October 1953) is an English-born chemist. He moved to the United States and began teaching at [[Illinois State University]] in 1984. Lash is known for his contributions to synthetic [[porphyrin]] chemistry.<ref name="TDLilli">{{cite web |title=Dr. Timothy Lash "Distinguished Professor, Organic Chemistry" |url=https://chemistry.illinoisstate.edu/faculty-staff/profile/?ulid=tdlash |website=chemistry.illinoisstate.edu |publisher=illinoisstate.edu}}</ref>

==Career==
Timothy D. Lash was born on 13 October 1953, in [[Salisbury]], England.<ref name="TDJ">{{cite journal |title=Recent Advances on the Synthesis and Chemistry of Carbaporphyrins and Related Porphyrinoid Systems |journal=European Journal of Organic Chemistry |date=November 2007 |volume=2007 |pages=5461–5481 |doi=10.1002/ejoc.200700478 |url=https://chemistry-europe.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/ejoc.200700478|last1=Lash |first1=Timothy D. |issue=33 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
He completed B.Sc. ''(Hon.)'' degree in chemistry from the [[University of Exeter]] in 1975 and his MS in organic chemistry from [[University of Wales]], College of Cardiff. In 1979 he received his Ph.D. in organic chemistry from same university under the guidance of A. H. Jackson.<ref name="TDLilli" /><ref name="TDJ" />

Lash joined the Department of Chemistry at [[Illinois State University]] in 1984 and assumed the rank of professor in 1993. In 2000, he was designated as a distinguished professor, the highest honor awarded by the university.<ref name="TDJ" /> In 2004, Lash was selected as “Chemist of the Year” for the Illinois Heartland section of the [[American Chemical Society]].<ref name="TDLilli"/>
